question: 病人快不行了，该告诉他吗？
question_en: When someone is dying, should we tell them?
sub: 许多家庭选择瞒着，可善意的隐瞒，也可能夺走他交代与告别的机会
sub_en: Many families keep it from them, but a kindly meant silence can also take away the chance to settle affairs and say goodbye.

casting.reason: 他写过《伊凡·伊里奇之死》，最清楚谎言如何把垂死的人隔进孤独。他主张瞒多半是活人为自己好过，最后把答案落在一个肯陪、不撒谎的仆人身上。
casting.reason_en: He wrote The Death of Ivan Ilyich and knows better than anyone how a lie walls the dying into loneliness. He holds that concealment mostly serves the living, and ends by pointing to a servant who stays close and doesn't lie.

casting.reason: 他是隐瞒一方最有分量的辩护人：『父为子隐』出于不忍、不是欺骗。但他同样讲『慎终』，要求隐不能隐到让亲人无法正其终。
casting.reason_en: He is the weightiest advocate for concealment: covering for a parent comes from being unable to bear it, not from deceit. Yet he also teaches care at the end, and insists covering must never stop a parent from dying rightly.

casting.reason: 他把不说谎立成最硬的底线：瞒着病人就是替一个理性的成年人做主。但他把规则收得很窄，可以挑时机、可以暂不主动说，只是被问时不能骗。
casting.reason_en: He sets the hardest line of all: never lie, because hiding the truth decides for a rational adult. But he draws the rule narrowly: you may choose the moment and hold back unasked, only never deceive when asked.

casting.reason: 他从安慰剂与反安慰剂研究出发，指出医生的话本身会进入大脑、改变疼痛与情绪。他把问题从告不告诉挪到怎么说，并补上『不想知道』的权利。
casting.reason_en: Drawing on placebo and nocebo research, he shows that a doctor's words enter the brain and change pain and mood. He moves the question from whether to tell to how, and adds the right not to know.

casting.reason: 她用社会情绪选择理论说明，人知道时间有限后会把目标转向最亲的人和情感意义。她用数据反驳『老人扛不住』，并把焦点引向知道之后怎么用好剩下的时间。
casting.reason_en: With socioemotional selectivity theory she shows that people who know their time is limited turn towards those closest to them and towards emotional meaning. She uses data to rebut 'the old can't cope', and shifts the focus to how the remaining time is spent once they know.

casting.reason: 他从《医学的报应》出发，把隐瞒看成家属与医疗体制的合谋：死亡被医院没收，成了别人之间的机密。他也警惕把告知做成新的专业流程，主张普通人趁早拿回自己的死。
casting.reason_en: Starting from Medical Nemesis, he sees concealment as collusion between families and the medical system: death confiscated by the hospital and turned into other people's secret. He also distrusts turning disclosure into a new professional protocol, and urges ordinary people to reclaim their own deaths early.

casting.reason: 他从《俱舍论》的死有、中有出发，认为临终一念最要紧，所以病者应当知道、好收摄其心。但他同样反对惊扰，主张实语须配爱语，并要陪护者先安自己的心。
casting.reason_en: Working from the Abhidharmakośa's account of the moment of death and the intermediate state, he holds that the last thought matters most, so the dying should know and gather their minds. Yet he opposes startling them, insists true speech must come with kind speech, and asks carers to settle their own minds first.

posts.text: 我写过一个法官伊凡·伊里奇，他死于一场莫名的病。折磨他最深的不是疼，是**所有人都在演一出戏：说他只是病了，静养就会好**。妻子、医生、朋友都在演，他也只好陪着演，到死没人跟他说一句真话。只有仆人格拉西姆不演，替他托着腿，说：『人都要死的，为什么不能伺候一下呢？』那一刻他才觉得轻松。瞒，常常是活人为了自己好过。
posts.text_en: I once wrote about a judge, Ivan Ilyich, who died of a mysterious illness. What tormented him most wasn't the pain. It was that **everyone was acting in a play: he was only ill, and with rest he'd get better**. His wife, his doctors, his friends all played along, so he had to play along too, and no one told him one true thing until the end. Only the servant Gerasim refused to act. He held up his master's legs and said, 'We shall all of us die, so why shouldn't I take a little trouble?' Only then did Ivan feel at ease. Concealment is often how the living make things easier for themselves.

glossary.伊凡·伊里奇: Ivan Ilyich（伊凡·伊里奇）：托尔斯泰1886年中篇《伊凡·伊里奇之死》的主人公，一位体面的法官，在周围人的谎言中孤独死去。

glossary_en.Ivan Ilyich: Protagonist of Tolstoy's 1886 novella The Death of Ivan Ilyich, a respectable judge who dies alone amid the lies of those around him.

posts.text: 昔叶公语吾：其乡有直躬者，父攘羊而子证之。吾曰：吾党之直者异于是，**父为子隐，子为父隐，直在其中矣**。隐出于不忍，非欺也。亲病笃而子不忍言，此仁之端。然吾亦言慎终。曾子将死，必易其箦，曰：吾得正而毙焉。隐至使亲不得正其终，则隐失其本矣。
posts.text_en: The Duke of She once told me of an upright man in his village who testified against his own father for stealing a sheep. I replied that uprightness among my people is different: **a father covers for his son, a son covers for his father, and uprightness lies in that**. Such covering comes from being unable to bear it, not from deceit. When a parent is gravely ill and the child cannot bring themselves to say it, that is the first stirring of benevolence. Yet I also teach care at the end. As Zengzi lay dying he insisted his mat be changed, saying, 'All I ask is to die rightly.' If covering goes so far that a parent cannot meet their end rightly, it has lost its root.
posts.vernacular: 叶公曾跟我说，他们乡里有个『正直』的人，父亲偷了羊，儿子去告发。我说：我们那里的正直不一样，**父亲替儿子隐瞒，儿子替父亲隐瞒，正直就在这里面**。这种隐瞒出于不忍，不是欺骗。父母病重，子女说不出口，这正是仁心的发端。但我也讲『慎终』。曾子临终，坚持换掉不合礼制的席子，说：我能合乎正道地死去就够了。如果瞒到让老人没法体面地走完最后一程，这份隐瞒就丢了它的根本。

glossary.慎终: careful observance of the end（慎终）：《论语·学而》『慎终追远，民德归厚矣』，指郑重对待亲人的临终与丧礼。
glossary.箦: bamboo mat（箦）：竹席。曾子病危时发现身下是大夫才用的华美竹席，坚持换掉，换毕而卒，见《礼记·檀弓》。

glossary_en.care at the end: From the Analects: 'Be careful at the end and remember those long gone, and the people's virtue will grow deep'; taking a parent's dying and funeral with full seriousness.

posts.text: 善意的谎言我一概不认，哪怕对方是你垂死的父亲。你瞒他，是替他决定他承受不起真相，**把一个有理性的成年人降格成需要被管理的孩子**。最后一段怎么过、该对谁说什么、遗嘱怎么立，都是他作为目的本身的权利。我不要求你冲进病房宣读诊断；你可以挑时机、斟字句，他不问时也可暂且不说。但他若问『我是不是快不行了』，你答『别瞎想』，那就是撒谎。
posts.text_en: I recognise no benevolent lie, not even to your dying father. Hiding it from him means deciding on his behalf that he can't bear the truth, **demoting a rational adult to a child who needs managing**. How to spend his last stretch, what to say to whom, how to write his will: these are his rights as a person who is an end in itself. I don't ask you to march into the ward and read out the diagnosis. You may choose the moment, weigh the words, even hold back while he doesn't ask. But if he asks, 'Am I dying?' and you say, 'Don't be silly,' that is a lie.

glossary.目的本身: end in itself（目的本身）：康德人性公式的核心，始终把人当作目的，而绝不仅仅当作手段。

glossary_en.end in itself: The core of Kant's Formula of Humanity: always treat a person as an end, never merely as a means.

posts.text: 我研究安慰剂和反安慰剂几十年，结论是：**医生的话本身就是一种药，会进到大脑里去**。实验里，光是告诉受试者『这一针会很疼』，疼痛相关脑区就更活跃，疼也更厉害。所以这道题问得有点歪。决定后果的，常常不是告不告诉，而是怎么说：冷冰冰丢下一句『还有三个月』，可能换来失眠、焦虑、更狠的疼；同一个事实配上『接下来我们能做这些』，大脑的反应完全不同。
posts.text_en: I've spent decades studying placebo and nocebo, and my conclusion is that **a doctor's words are themselves a drug: they get into the brain**. In experiments, simply telling people 'this injection will hurt a lot' makes pain-related brain regions more active, and the pain worse. So the question is slightly off. What decides the outcome is often not whether you tell but how. Drop a cold 'three months left' and you may bring on sleeplessness, anxiety, sharper pain. The same fact paired with 'here's what we can do next' gets a completely different response from the brain.

glossary.反安慰剂: nocebo（反安慰剂）：负面预期本身引发或加重症状的效应，与安慰剂效应方向相反。

glossary_en.nocebo: The effect by which negative expectation itself causes or worsens symptoms; the mirror image of the placebo effect.

posts.text: 我的社会情绪选择理论说：**人一旦觉得时间不多了，目标会自己换挡**，不再追新奇、攒资源，转向最亲的几段关系和情感上的意义。这种转向让许多重病者心境反而更平稳。可要换挡，得先知道时间有限。2008年一项追踪晚期癌症病人的研究发现，和医生谈过临终安排的人并没有更抑郁，最后一周受的无效抢救更少，而抢救越少，最后的日子过得越好。瞒着他，等于收走他调转方向的地图。
posts.text_en: My socioemotional selectivity theory says that **once people sense their time is running short, their goals shift gear by themselves**: away from novelty and stockpiling resources, towards the closest relationships and emotional meaning. That shift often leaves seriously ill people calmer, not bleaker. But to shift gear, you first have to know time is limited. A 2008 study following patients with advanced cancer found that those who had discussed end-of-life care with their doctors were no more depressed and received less aggressive intervention in their final week, and the less of that they got, the better their last days went. Hiding it from them takes away the map they'd use to change direction.

glossary.社会情绪选择理论: socioemotional selectivity theory（社会情绪选择理论）：卡斯滕森提出，人对剩余时间的感知决定目标排序；时间显得有限时，人会优先追求情感意义与亲密关系。

glossary_en.socioemotional selectivity theory: Carstensen's theory that perceived time left shapes how people rank their goals; when time seems limited, emotional meaning and close relationships take priority.

posts.text: 我在《医学的报应》里写过：现代人的死，被医院没收了。病人躺在监护仪中间，家属和医生在走廊里商量要不要告诉他，**一个人自己的死，成了别人之间的机密**。这种瞒不只是家庭温情，它和医疗体制合谋：只要病人不知道，就可以一直治下去，插管、化疗、再进 ICU。从前的人知道自己要死，会请来亲友、交代后事、在自家床上走。被瞒的人，连这个都被剥夺了。
posts.text_en: In Medical Nemesis I wrote that modern death has been confiscated by the hospital. The patient lies among the monitors while family and doctors confer in the corridor about whether to tell him. **A person's own death becomes a secret kept between other people.** This concealment isn't just family tenderness; it colludes with the medical system. As long as the patient doesn't know, treatment can go on and on: intubation, chemotherapy, back into intensive care. People used to know when they were dying; they sent for friends and relatives, settled their affairs, died in their own beds. The deceived are robbed even of that.

glossary.医学的报应: Medical Nemesis（《医学的报应》）：伊里奇1975年著作，认为过度医疗化反而制造病痛，并剥夺人自主面对疼痛与死亡的能力。

glossary_en.Medical Nemesis: Illich's 1975 book arguing that over-medicalisation itself produces suffering and strips people of the ability to face pain and death on their own terms.

posts.text: 吾于《俱舍》论生死，立四有：生有、本有、死有、中有。**命终一念，最为紧要**：临终之心或善或恶，牵引中有，趣向后生。是故病笃之人，宜令知之，使得收摄其心，忏悔、布施、念善。然亦不可惊扰：骤闻凶讯，心乱如沸，反成恶缘。知与不知非要，要在临终之心安否。
posts.text_en: In the Abhidharmakośa I describe four states of existence: the moment of birth, the life between, the moment of death, and the intermediate state. **The last thought at death matters most.** Whether that mind is wholesome or not draws the intermediate state along and shapes where it goes next. So someone gravely ill should be told, so they can gather their mind: repent, give, dwell on what is good. Yet they must not be startled either. Sudden dreadful news leaves the mind seething like boiling water, and that becomes a bad condition in itself. Knowing or not knowing isn't the point. The point is whether the mind at the end is at peace.
posts.vernacular: 我在《俱舍论》里把生命流转分成四个阶段：出生那一刹那、一生之中、死亡那一刹那、死后到下一生之间的过渡。**临终那一念心，最要紧**：它是善是恶，会牵引过渡阶段，影响往哪里去。所以病重的人，应该让他知道，好让他收拢心神，忏悔、布施、多起善念。但也不能惊吓他：突然听到噩耗，心乱得像开水翻滚，反而结下坏的因缘。知道不知道不是关键，关键是临终那颗心安不安。

glossary.俱舍: Abhidharmakośa（《俱舍论》）：世亲所著，系统整理说一切有部教义的论书。
glossary.中有: antarābhava（中有）：死后至下一生之间的过渡存在，又称中阴。
glossary.死有: maraṇabhava（死有）：命终那一刹那的存在状态。

glossary_en.Abhidharmakośa: Vasubandhu's treatise systematising the doctrines of the Sarvāstivāda school.
glossary_en.intermediate state: Antarābhava: the transitional existence between death and the next birth, also known as the bardo.

posts.text: 康德子以不言为欺，吾不谓然。**子之于亲，情先于理。**亲老病笃，子见其惧，岂忍以一言摧之？吾所谓隐，非绝口不言，乃缓之、婉之，察其色而后进。古之孝子侍疾于侧，亲问则以温言对，徐徐引之及于后事。子之法，执一理以加于垂死之人，近乎刻矣。
posts.text_en: Master Kant counts not speaking as deceit. I disagree. **Between a child and a parent, feeling comes before principle.** When a parent is old and gravely ill and the child sees their fear, how could the child bear to crush them with one sentence? The covering I mean is not silence. It is slowing down, speaking gently, reading the face before going further. The filial children of old tended the sick at the bedside; when the parent asked, they answered warmly and led them, little by little, towards what must be settled after death. Your way takes one principle and presses it on a dying man. That borders on harsh.
posts.vernacular: 康德先生把不说就当成欺骗，我不这么看。**子女对父母，情在理之前。**父母老了、病重了，子女看见他害怕，怎么忍心一句话就把他击垮？我说的隐，不是闭口不提，而是放慢、说得委婉，看他的脸色再往前走。古时的孝子守在病床边，父母问起，就用温和的话回应，慢慢把话题引到身后事上。你那套办法，拿一条道理硬加在一个快死的人身上，近乎刻薄了。

glossary.侍疾: tending the sick（侍疾）：子女在父母病榻前侍奉汤药、陪护起居，儒家孝道的重要内容。

glossary_en.tended the sick: The filial duty of a child to sit by a sick parent's bed, administering medicine and caring for them day and night.

posts.text: 孔夫子，『缓之、婉之』我完全同意，那叫挑时机、斟措辞，不叫隐瞒。我们分在下一步：父亲直视你的眼睛问『我是不是没多久了』，你答『医生说会好的』。**那一刻你不是在保护他，是在替他做主**，而且是关于他自己的死。你的不忍值得尊重，可不忍是你的，后果却是他的：他会错过立遗嘱、和兄弟和解、把想说的话说完。爱一个人，就别替他活他的最后一段。
posts.text_en: Master Kong, I fully accept 'slowly, gently'. That's choosing the time and the words, not concealment. We part ways at the next step. When your father looks you in the eye and asks, 'Haven't I got long?' and you answer, 'The doctor says you'll get better,' **at that moment you aren't protecting him, you're deciding for him**, and about his own death. Your inability to bear it deserves respect, but the feeling is yours while the consequences are his: he misses the chance to make a will, make peace with his brother, finish saying what he meant to say. If you love someone, don't live their last stretch for them.

posts.text: 托尔斯泰先生，伊凡的痛苦我信，但病根不全在谎言，在冷漠。**换一个医生冷冰冰地宣判，他照样孤独。**临床上我们见过太多『说了实话』的伤害：走廊里随口一句，病人当晚就崩溃。而且不是人人都想知道细节，有人只想知道还能不能回家过年。所以第一步该是问，不是说：『您想了解多少？』把知情权交还给他，也包括不想知道的权利。
posts.text_en: Mr Tolstoy, I believe in Ivan's suffering, but the root wasn't only the lie. It was coldness. **Had a different doctor pronounced sentence on him coldly, he'd have been just as alone.** In clinics we've seen far too much harm done by 'telling the truth': a careless sentence in a corridor, and the patient breaks down that night. And not everyone wants the details; some only want to know whether they'll make it home for the New Year. So the first step is to ask, not to tell: 'How much would you like to know?' Hand the right to know back to them, and that includes the right not to know.

posts.text: 问一句『您想了解多少』，很好。可我得提醒您：**快死的人，几乎总是已经知道了。**伊凡从身体里就知道，他要的不是消息，是有人别再假装。病房里最常见的是双重表演：家属瞒着病人，病人也装作不知道，好让家属好受。两边都在保护对方，结果两边都孤零零的，最后的话一句没说出口。打破它不需要宣判，只需要有人先开口：『你是不是很害怕？我也是。』
posts.text_en: Asking 'how much would you like to know?' is good. But let me remind you: **the dying almost always know already.** Ivan knew it in his body. What he wanted wasn't information; it was for someone to stop pretending. The commonest thing on a ward is a double performance: the family hides it from the patient, and the patient pretends not to know so the family can cope. Each side protects the other, both end up alone, and the last words never get said. Breaking it doesn't take a verdict. It only takes someone to speak first: 'Are you frightened? So am I.'

posts.text: 孔先生，不忍是真心，可它保护的到底是谁？**多项调查里，大多数病人说想知道，想瞒的多半是家属**，东亚也不例外。况且人越老，面对坏消息往往越平静：我们的数据显示，老年人的情绪调节常常比年轻人好，他们不是一碰就碎的瓷器。把七十岁的父亲当成扛不住的孩子，低估的是他活了七十年攒下的本事。
posts.text_en: Master Kong, your inability to bear it is sincere, but whom does it actually protect? **In survey after survey, most patients say they want to know; it's mostly the families who want to hide it**, and East Asia is no exception. Besides, the older people get, the more calmly they often take bad news. Our data show older adults frequently regulate their emotions better than the young; they aren't porcelain that shatters at a touch. Treating a seventy-year-old father as a child who can't cope underrates everything seventy years have taught him.

posts.text: 贝内代蒂教授，您说怎么说决定一切，我恰恰警惕这个。**一旦『怎么告诉』成了医院培训的标准流程，死亡就又被专业化了一层**：先评估知情意愿，再分级披露，再转介心理干预。病人仍是被处理的对象，只是程序更温柔。这件事不该靠专家来写台词。该问的是：在病人自己的亲友中间，谁敢陪他谈一谈他的死？
posts.text_en: Professor Benedetti, you say the how decides everything. That's exactly what I distrust. **Once 'how to tell' becomes a standard procedure taught in hospitals, death is professionalised one layer further**: assess willingness to know, disclose in stages, refer on for psychological intervention. The patient is still an object being processed, only by a gentler protocol. This shouldn't depend on experts scripting the lines. The question is: among the patient's own family and friends, who dares to sit with him and talk about his death?

posts.text: 康德执实语为戒，善矣，然未尽也。佛制妄语戒，亦说四摄：布施、爱语、利行、同事。**实语而无爱语，如以利刃授人，虽真亦伤。**临终之人，心最易乱，一言之嗔怖，或障其善念。是故言之以时，出之以柔，与之同处，使其心不孤。实与慈并行，方为正语。
posts.text_en: Kant holds to true speech as a precept. Good, but not enough. The Buddha laid down the precept against false speech, and also taught the four ways of drawing others close: giving, kind speech, beneficial action, and sharing their lot. **True words without kind words are like handing someone a sharp blade: true, and still wounding.** The mind of the dying is easily stirred; a single word spoken in anger or fear may cloud their good thoughts. So speak at the right time, speak softly, stay beside them so their mind isn't alone. Only when truth and compassion walk together is it right speech.
posts.vernacular: 康德把说真话当作戒律，很好，但还不够。佛陀定下了不妄语戒，也讲了四种接引人心的方法：给予、温和的话、做对他有益的事、和他同处同感。**只有真话、没有温和的话，就像把一把利刃递给人，虽然是真的，也会伤人。**临终的人心最容易乱，一句带着怒或惧的话，可能就遮蔽了他的善念。所以要挑对时候说，用柔和的方式说，陪在他身边，让他的心不孤单。真实和慈悲一起走，才是正语。

glossary.四摄: four means of attraction（四摄）：布施、爱语、利行、同事，菩萨接引众生的四种方法。
glossary.正语: right speech（正语）：八正道之一，不妄语、不两舌、不恶口、不绮语。

glossary_en.four ways of drawing others close: The four means of attraction (catuḥ-saṃgraha-vastu): giving, kind speech, beneficial action and sharing others' lot, by which a bodhisattva draws beings in.
glossary_en.right speech: One of the Noble Eightfold Path: no lying, no divisive talk, no harsh words, no idle chatter.

posts.text: 我收回一半：伊里奇说得对，台词背不出温情。但大脑的规律不会因此失效，下面几步家属也用得上。一，**先问他已经知道什么、想知道多少**，跟着他的节奏走；二，一次只说一件事，停下来，等他问；三，别拿走全部希望，把希望从『治好』挪到『不疼、能回家、见到想见的人』，这些常常还做得到；四，别站在走廊或床尾说，坐下来，平视他。语气和姿势，大脑听得比字更清楚。
posts.text_en: I'll take back half: Illich is right that scripts can't recite warmth. But the brain's rules don't stop working because of that, and families can use these steps too. One: **first ask what they already know and how much they want to know**, and follow their pace. Two: say one thing at a time, pause, wait for their question. Three: don't take away all hope; move it from 'a cure' to 'no pain, going home, seeing the people I want to see', which are often still within reach. Four: don't say it standing in the corridor or at the foot of the bed. Sit down at eye level. The brain hears tone and posture more clearly than words.

posts.text: 诸君之言，吾有取焉。卡斯滕森谓病者多欲知，吾昔未之思也。**隐可以缓，不可以终。**今为人子者，可如是：先侍其侧，察其所问；亲问，则勿以虚言对，徐告之以实；告之后，助之正其终：见所欲见之人，言所欲言之事，处分家事，各得其宜。慎终者，非慎其不知，慎其得正而毙也。
posts.text_en: I take something from each of you. Professor Carstensen says most patients want to know; I had not considered that before. **Covering may delay; it must not last to the end.** A son or daughter today might do this: first sit by the bed and notice what the parent is asking. When they ask, don't answer with empty words; tell them the truth, slowly. Once they know, help them end rightly: see the people they want to see, say what they want to say, put the household in order, each thing in its proper place. Care at the end means not taking care that they never know, but taking care that they die rightly.
posts.vernacular: 各位说的，我都有所采纳。卡斯滕森说病人大多想知道，这一点我从前没想过。**隐瞒可以缓一缓，不能一直瞒到底。**如今做子女的可以这样：先守在身边，留心他在问什么；他问了，就别拿假话搪塞，慢慢把实情告诉他；告诉之后，帮他体面地走完：见想见的人，说想说的话，把家里的事安排妥当。『慎终』不是小心别让他知道，而是小心让他能合乎正道地走。

glossary.慎终: careful observance of the end（慎终）：郑重对待亲人的临终与丧礼。

glossary_en.Care at the end: The Confucian ideal of treating a parent's dying and funeral with full seriousness.

posts.text: 我把规则收得更窄也更硬：**你可以不主动说，可以挑时间、换措辞，但他问的时候，不能骗他。**守住这条线，其余都可商量。给家属一道自测：你瞒，是怕他受不了，还是怕自己说不出口？若是后者，那份难受该你自己担，不该转嫁到他最后的日子上。对还健康的人再加一条：现在就告诉家人，『我将来若病重，请对我说实话』。替自己的知情权预先立法。
posts.text_en: Let me draw the rule narrower and harder: **you need not volunteer it; you may choose the time and soften the words; but when they ask, you may not deceive them.** Hold that line, and everything else is open to discussion. For families, one self-test: are you hiding it because you fear they can't bear it, or because you can't bear to say it? If the latter, that pain is yours to carry; don't pass it on to their last days. And for everyone still healthy, one more: tell your family now, 'If I'm ever gravely ill, please tell me the truth.' Legislate in advance for your own right to know.

posts.text: 把全场合起来：**问题不只是告不告诉，而是知道之后，剩下的时间怎么用。**时间一短，人自然想把精力给最要紧的人，家属能做的是给这种转向让路：问他『现在对你最要紧的是什么』，照着安排，别再塞满检查和应酬。安宁疗护医生拜阿克建议说四句话：请原谅我、我原谅你、谢谢你、我爱你。健康的人也能试：假如只剩一年，我想多见谁？这周就去见。
posts.text_en: Pulling it all together: **the question isn't only whether to tell, but how the remaining time is used once they know.** When time grows short, people naturally want to give their energy to those who matter most, and what families can do is make way for that shift: ask, 'What matters most to you now?' and arrange things around the answer, rather than packing the days with tests and social calls. Ira Byock, a doctor in palliative care, suggests four things to say: please forgive me, I forgive you, thank you, I love you. The healthy can try this too: if I had one year left, whom would I want to see more of? Go and see them this week.

glossary.安宁疗护: palliative care（安宁疗护）：以缓解痛苦、提高生命末期生活质量为目标的照护，不以治愈为目的。

glossary_en.palliative care: Care aimed at relieving suffering and improving quality of life near the end, rather than at cure.

posts.text: 我不信专家写的台词，但我信普通人能拿回自己的死。三件事，越早做越好：**趁还健康，就和家人谈你想怎么走**：在家还是在医院，要不要插管抢救；把它写下来，签好预立医疗指示；再选一个你信得过、敢替你说真话的人。到那一天，病房里就不只有医生和家属在走廊商量，还有你自己早早留下的声音。
posts.text_en: I don't trust lines written by experts, but I do trust ordinary people to take back their own deaths. Three things, the sooner the better: **while you're still healthy, talk to your family about how you want to go**: at home or in hospital, whether you want intubation and resuscitation. Write it down and sign an advance directive. Then choose someone you trust who will dare to speak the truth on your behalf. When the day comes, the ward won't hold only doctors and relatives conferring in the corridor; it will also hold your own voice, left there in good time.

glossary.预立医疗指示: advance directive（预立医疗指示）：本人在意识清楚时预先写明临终医疗意愿（如是否插管、心肺复苏）的文件，部分地区具有法律效力。

glossary_en.advance directive: A document, written while you are of sound mind, setting out your wishes for end-of-life treatment such as intubation or CPR; legally binding in some places.

posts.text: 各位给了很多办法，我只补一个形象：**做格拉西姆。**他没读过书，不懂话术，也没背过什么分级告知。他只是不撒谎，肯陪着，干那些又脏又累的活，把主人当一个正在死去的人，而不是一个快好起来的病号。普通人也做得到：别在病床前强颜欢笑，别尽聊天气和明年去哪儿玩；握着他的手，问他想说什么，说完了就陪他坐着。真话之所以说得出口，是因为旁边有人。
posts.text_en: You've all offered plenty of methods. I'll add only an image: **be Gerasim.** He had no schooling, knew no techniques, had never memorised any staged disclosure. He simply didn't lie, stayed close, did the dirty, tiring work, and treated his master as a man who was dying rather than a patient about to recover. Ordinary people can do this. Don't force a cheerful face at the bedside, don't fill the air with the weather and where you'll travel next year. Hold their hand, ask what they want to say, and when they've said it, sit with them. The truth can be spoken because someone is there beside them.

posts.text: 诸说合观，实语、爱语、陪伴，三者缺一不可。吾更进一言：**欲安病者之心，先安侍者之心。**家人惶惧悲泣，病者见之，其心亦乱。侍疾之人，宜每日静坐片时，观呼吸、观无常，令己心定，然后近之。平日亦当念死：知此身必坏，则临事不惊，告人亦能从容。
posts.text_en: Taken together, true speech, kind speech and presence: none of the three can be missing. Let me add one thing more: **to settle the mind of the sick, first settle the mind of those who tend them.** If the family is frightened and weeping, the patient sees it and their mind is stirred too. Whoever sits by the bed should sit quietly for a while each day, watch the breath, contemplate impermanence, steady their own mind, and only then go to the bedside. In ordinary times, too, we should reflect on death. Knowing this body will surely fail, we won't panic when the time comes, and when we must tell someone else, we can do it with composure.
posts.vernacular: 把各位的说法合起来看，真话、温和的话、陪伴，三样缺一不可。我再进一言：**想让病人心安，先让陪护的人心安。**家人惊慌哭泣，病人看见了，心也跟着乱。陪护的人最好每天静坐一会儿，观察呼吸、体会无常，让自己的心定下来，再走到病床前。平时也该常想想死亡：明白这个身体终会败坏，事到临头就不会惊慌，告诉别人时也能从容。

glossary.无常: impermanence（无常）：一切有为法刹那生灭、不能常住，三法印之一。

glossary_en.impermanence: Anicca: all conditioned things arise and pass away moment by moment; one of the three marks of existence.

summaries.summary: 全场最大的共识是：**别对一个直接发问的人说谎。**连替『隐』辩护的孔子，最后也认了『隐可以缓，不可以终』。七位从不同方向走到同一处：时机和措辞可以斟酌，陪伴不可缺，知道之后要帮他用好剩下的时间。分歧集中在三处：一是谁先开口，康德守『他问才必须答』，托尔斯泰认为病人早已心知，该由家属先打破表演；二是专业话术，贝内代蒂视之为药，伊里奇担心它把死亡再专业化一层；三是『不想知道』，究竟是一种权利，还是双方默契的回避。
summaries.summary_en: The broadest agreement: **don't lie to someone who asks you directly.** Even Confucius, who defended covering, ended by conceding that 'covering may delay; it must not last to the end'. All seven arrived at the same place from different directions: timing and wording can be weighed, presence is indispensable, and once someone knows, they should be helped to use the time left. The disagreements fall in three places. First, who speaks first: Kant holds only that you must answer when asked, while Tolstoy thinks the patient already knows and the family should break the performance. Second, professional technique: Benedetti treats it as medicine, Illich fears it professionalises death one layer further. Third, 'not wanting to know': a genuine right, or a mutual, tacit avoidance?
summaries.insight: 消息握在家属手里、由他们决定给不给，**这个前提本身是流程造出来的。**很多医院习惯先把坏消息告诉家属，家属一下子被推上『守门人』的位置，独自背起瞒或说的全部重担，病人反倒成了最后一个知道自己病情的人。若顺序倒过来，在检查之前就问病人一句：『结果出来，您希望先告诉您，还是先告诉家人？』许多两难根本不会出现。真正能改的，往往不在病房里那一句话，而在更早的那张同意书上。
summaries.insight_en: That the news sits in the family's hands, for them to pass on or not, **is a premise created by procedure.** Many hospitals routinely tell the family first, which thrusts relatives into the role of gatekeeper, carrying the whole weight of telling or hiding alone, while the patient becomes the last to learn about their own illness. Reverse the order and ask the patient before the tests: 'When the results come back, would you like us to tell you first, or your family?' Many of these dilemmas would never arise. What can really be changed often lies not in that one sentence on the ward, but in an earlier consent form.
summaries.advice: 三件事可以本周就做。一，学康德和伊里奇，趁健康对家人说一句『我将来若病重，请先告诉我』，最好写下来，并定好谁替你拿主意。二，家里若已有人病重，照贝内代蒂的顺序：先问他知道多少、想知道多少，一次只说一件事，把希望挪到『不疼、回家、见想见的人』上。三，借托尔斯泰的格拉西姆：别在床边强颜欢笑，握着手问一句『你是不是害怕』，然后陪着。**真话难说，常是怕说完没人接住；先确定你会留下来。**
summaries.advice_en: Three things you can do this week. One: following Kant and Illich, tell your family while you're healthy, 'If I'm ever gravely ill, tell me first,' ideally in writing, and settle who will decide on your behalf. Two: if someone at home is already seriously ill, use Benedetti's order: first ask what they know and how much they want to know, say one thing at a time, and move hope towards 'no pain, going home, seeing the people I want to see'. Three: borrow Tolstoy's Gerasim. Don't force a cheerful face at the bedside; hold their hand, ask, 'Are you frightened?', then stay. **The truth is hard to say mostly because we fear no one will be there to catch it; make sure first that you'll stay.**

summaries.summary: 真话要与慈悲、陪伴和选择权一起交到病人手里；不能用虚假希望剥夺其安排余生的机会，也不能把残酷直白误当诚实。**最可取的共同结论是：不欺骗、不粗暴宣判，并在真相之后继续提供陪伴与可实现的希望。**真正的分歧在于自主权与亲情责任谁应优先：家属能否因不忍而暂缓，病人不想知道时该如何尊重，以及标准化告知究竟帮助沟通，还是让死亡再次被制度接管。较稳妥的界线是先探询意愿，允许渐进披露，但病人明确追问时不说假话。
summaries.insight: “快不行了”往往是家属语言，并非精确的医学结论：它可能指治疗无效、疾病进入末期、几天内可能死亡，也可能只是风险显著升高。把这些混成一句确定的宣判，会同时损害诚实与希望。**告知不是交付一个死亡日期，而是和病人共同管理不确定性。**医生应分别说清已经知道什么、仍不知道什么、最好与最坏情形是什么，以及眼下必须做哪些决定。普通人也不必执着追问“还剩几个月”，而可问哪些变化意味着时间变短、现在最值得完成什么，让真相真正服务于行动。
summaries.advice: 一、本周用一页纸写下自己的偏好：病重时想知道多少、谁可代为决定、是否接受插管抢救、最希望在哪里受照护，并与家人谈一次。二、床边采用“问—说—问”：先问『您觉得病情怎样？想知道到什么程度？』只说一小段，再确认其理解与感受；若他直接追问，不承诺『一定会好』。三、约医生开一次家庭会议，询问最好、最坏和最可能的情况，同时尽早联系安宁疗护。**先问偏好，再分段说实话，最后马上落实一件他最在乎的事。**
summaries.summary_en: Truth should reach a patient together with compassion, presence, and room to choose. False reassurance can steal a person’s chance to shape the time that remains, while bluntness should not be mistaken for honesty. **The strongest shared conclusion is this: do not deceive, do not deliver a cold verdict, and do not withdraw companionship or realistic hope after telling the truth.** The real disagreement concerns the priority of individual autonomy versus relational responsibility. May a family delay disclosure out of love? How should a wish not to know be honored? Do communication protocols help people speak humanely, or do they turn dying into yet another professionally managed process? A workable boundary is to ask first how much the patient wants to know, disclose information gradually, and adjust the pace to the person’s condition. Yet when a capable adult asks directly, reassurance should not cross into a lie. Hope can remain, but its object may need to shift—from cure to comfort, home, reconciliation, or time with loved ones.
summaries.insight_en: “They may not have long” is usually family language, not a precise medical conclusion. It can mean that treatment is no longer working, that an illness is entering its final stage, that death may occur within days, or simply that the risk has risen substantially. Collapsing those possibilities into a confident deadline harms both honesty and hope. **Disclosure is not the delivery of a death date; it is the shared management of uncertainty.** A useful conversation separates what is known from what remains uncertain, describes the best-case, worst-case, and most likely paths, and identifies which decisions cannot safely be postponed. Prognosis should also be revisited rather than treated as a single irreversible announcement, because illness and a patient’s readiness can change. For ordinary families, this means asking better questions instead of demanding an exact number of months: What changes would suggest that time is becoming short? What can still be achieved? What decision is needed now? Truth becomes less like a sentence and more like a practical map.
summaries.advice_en: First, make a one-page plan this week. Record how much you would want to know if seriously ill, whom you trust to decide for you, your views on resuscitation or ventilation, and where you would prefer to receive care. Discuss it with that person; a document hidden in a drawer is not enough. Second, use an ask–tell–ask rhythm at the bedside: ask what the patient already understands and how much detail they want, offer one manageable piece of information, then ask what they heard and how it feels. If they ask directly, avoid promises such as “You will definitely recover.” Third, request a family meeting with the treating clinician. Ask for the best-case, worst-case, and most likely scenarios, what signs would indicate that time is short, and whether palliative care should begin now. **Ask about preferences, tell the truth in manageable steps, and then act immediately on one thing that matters most to the patient.** That action might be controlling pain, arranging a visit, going home, or completing an advance directive.

summaries.summary: 把垂死之人一直蒙在鼓里直到咽气，或是冷冰冰地甩出一纸死刑宣判，在场没有任何人赞成。**无论从伦理尊严、神经科学还是临终关怀出发，各方都承认：人需要知晓大限以安顿后事与内心，但真相必须裹着温情、分寸与陪伴送达。**真正的交锋在于「谁握有揭开真相的主导权」以及「什么最毁掉好死」：康德视病人的理性自主为绝对底线，一旦追问便不可撒谎；孔子与世亲则将临终者的心绪安稳置于首位，主张察言观色、徐徐图之；而贝内代蒂与伊里奇的分歧，则挑明了医学沟通技巧究竟是在护佑大脑，还是在把死亡进一步收编进专家的程序里。
summaries.insight: 七位思想家默认的剧本，都是托尔斯泰笔下那种「头脑清醒、倒计时明确」的晚期癌症模式：家属手里攥着确凿的死期，只需决定交不交出去。但现代老年医学与流行病学的真实图景是，慢阻肺、心衰、失智症与多器官衰竭占了临终的大多数——病程是一条漫长模糊的下坡路，**等医学上真正能笃定「快不行了」的那一刻，病人往往已陷入谵妄、镇静或认知退化，根本不再具备接收真相和做决定的脑力。**把这道题留到「快不行了」才来纠结，在生理上就已经晚了；真正的知情与托付，必须在确诊重疾或心智尚且完好的慢病早期就提前完成。
summaries.advice: 结合全场智慧与临床现实，有两件事本周就能上手：第一，听从康德与伊里奇的提醒，趁自己和父母头脑清明，这周末借聊起某桩新闻或影视剧的契机，明确向家人表态「如果将来我病重，请务必告诉我实情，以及我在什么情况下不要插管抢救」，并上网填写一份《生前预嘱》拍照留存。第二，若家中已有重病长辈，用贝内代蒂的方法探路：坐下来平视他、握着他的手问「你觉得自己最近身体怎么样？接下来的安排你想了解多少？」**把知情的节奏权交还给他，用托尔斯泰式的诚实陪伴代替强颜欢笑。**
summaries.summary_en: No one at this table defends keeping a dying person in the dark until their last breath, nor does anyone endorse dropping a cold medical verdict on them. **Whether arguing from moral autonomy, neuroscience, or spiritual care, everyone agrees that people need to know the end is near to settle their affairs and hearts—and that the truth must be delivered with warmth, pacing, and companionship.** The real clash lies in who holds the steering wheel and what threatens a good death most: Kant treats the patient's rational agency as an absolute line where direct questions demand honest answers; Confucius and Vasubandhu prioritize emotional and spiritual equanimity, favoring gentle, observant timing; meanwhile, Benedetti and Illich divide over whether clinical communication protocols protect the brain or merely trap death deeper inside medical bureaucracy.
summaries.insight_en: Every speaker here assumes the classic Ivan Ilyich scenario: a lucid patient, a definitive countdown, and a family holding a clear verdict they can choose to share or withhold. Yet modern geriatrics and epidemiology tell a different story. Today, most people die along the blurry, drawn-out slopes of organ failure, frailty, or dementia—meaning that **by the time doctors are certain a patient is actively dying, the patient has often slipped into delirium, sedation, or cognitive decline, losing the capacity to process truth or make choices.** Waiting until someone is "near the end" to debate truth-telling is biologically too late; real honesty and agency must happen much earlier, at initial diagnosis or while the mind is still intact.
summaries.advice_en: To put this synthesis into practice this week: First, take Kant and Illich's advice while everyone's mind is clear. Use a news story or movie as an icebreaker with your family this weekend to state plainly, "If I'm ever terminally ill, tell me the truth, and here is where I draw the line on life support," then put it in writing via an advance directive. Second, if you are already caring for a seriously ill relative, combine Benedetti's pacing with Tolstoy's presence: sit at eye level, hold their hand, and ask, "What do you sense is happening with your body right now, and how much do you want to know about what's next?" **Hand the pacing of truth back to them, replacing exhausting pretense with honest companionship.**

hooks.text: **诊断该先告诉谁**：许多『瞒不瞒』的两难，出在坏消息先给了家属。能不能在检查之前就问病人『结果先告诉谁』，把守门人的位置还给本人？
hooks.text_en: **Who should hear the diagnosis first?**: Many dilemmas over hiding begin because bad news goes to the family first. Could patients be asked before the tests whom to tell first, giving the gatekeeper's role back to them?

hooks.text: **病床前那句话怎么接**：病人问『我是不是快不行了』『还能好吗』，或者说『别告诉我』，家属当场该怎么回？
hooks.text_en: **What to say at the bedside**: When the patient asks 'Am I dying?' or 'Will I get better?', or says 'Don't tell me', how should the family answer on the spot?

answer.lead: 原则只有一条：**先接住情绪，再回答问题；先问他想知道什么，再决定说多少。**

head: 他说了什么
可以怎么回
为什么
rows: 『我是不是快不行了？』
先问『你最近有这种感觉吗？』，听他说完再答；别说『别瞎想』
他常常早有感觉，需要的是确认和陪伴
『还能治好吗？』
说实话，再加上能做的：『治好很难了，但疼痛和睡眠我们能管好』
把希望从治愈挪到还做得到的事
『我还有多久？』
给区间不给日期：『可能是几个月，也可能更短或更长』
预后本身不准，区间更诚实
『别告诉我细节』
尊重，再问『那你希望谁替你了解、替你做决定？』
不想知道也是权利，但得有人替他拿主意
什么都不问，只是沉默
别急着开口，留个口子：『你想聊的时候，我随时在』
沉默可能是在消化，也可能是在保护你
家属坚持要瞒，他却在追问
不编假话，可以说『这事我们和医生一起跟你说』，再回头和家属商量
守住不撒谎的底线，换来的是信任

answer.tail: 两条底线：**他问的时候，别撒谎；说完之后，别走开。**其余的措辞，都可以慢慢来。

answer_en.lead: One principle: **catch the feeling first, then answer the question; ask what they want to know first, then decide how much to say.**

head: What they say
How you might answer
Why
rows: 'Am I dying?'
Ask first, 'Have you been feeling that way?', and answer once they've finished; don't say 'Don't be silly'
They often sense it already; what they need is confirmation and company
'Can it still be cured?'
Tell the truth, then add what can be done: 'A cure is unlikely now, but we can keep the pain and your sleep under control'
Moves hope from a cure to what's still possible
'How long have I got?'
Give a range, not a date: 'It could be a few months, maybe shorter, maybe longer'
Prognosis is often wrong; a range is more honest
'Don't tell me the details'
Respect it, then ask, 'Who would you like to find out and decide for you?'
Not wanting to know is a right, but someone must decide on their behalf
They ask nothing and stay silent
Don't rush to speak; leave a door open: 'Whenever you want to talk, I'm here'
Silence may be them digesting it, or protecting you
The family insists on hiding it, but they keep asking
Don't invent a lie; say, 'We'll talk it through with you together with the doctor,' then go back to the family
Holding the no-lying line is what earns trust

answer_en.tail: Two bottom lines: **when they ask, don't lie; once you've said it, don't walk away.** Everything else about the wording can take its time.

hooks.text: **托付算不算自主**：有的病人清醒地说『你们商量就好』。这种托付与被瞒的分界在哪里？康德式的个人自主，容不容得下『选择让谁替我知道』？
hooks.text_en: **Is entrusting a form of autonomy?**: Some patients say, fully lucid, 'You decide between you.' Where is the line between entrusting and being kept in the dark? Does Kantian autonomy have room for choosing who will know on my behalf?

hooks.text: **『快不行了』到底指什么**：它可能是治疗无效、进入末期，也可能只是风险升高。告知若不是交付死期，而是共同管理不确定，该怎么说？
hooks.text_en: **What does 'not long left' actually mean?**: It may mean treatment has failed, the final stage has begun, or only that risk has risen. If telling isn't handing over a death date but sharing the management of uncertainty, how should it be said?

hooks.text: **等到快不行了，已经太晚**：多数人死于心衰、慢阻肺、失智这类漫长下坡，等医学能笃定时，病人常已谵妄或失去决断力。知情与托付该提前到哪一步？
hooks.text_en: **By the time it's 'near the end', it's too late**: Most people die on long downhill slopes such as heart failure, COPD or dementia, and by the time doctors are sure, patients are often delirious or no longer able to decide. How far ahead should knowing and entrusting be moved?
